title: Rip Roberts and the San Jacinto club
summary: He does not recall recording for Rip Roberts but knew him and his partner Webber from playing at his club.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Do you remember- I remember a guy named Rip Roberts? Remember Rip Roberts? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. He did- he did one record for Rip. That one record. It was called, uh, Long-Hairs- Long-Hairs Boogie. Ballin' with Fess. And- what was the name? There was a flip side. You know it. I can't think. Got a whole lot of love for you. Got a whole-

I don't remember ever doing anything for Rip Roberts. You know Rip Roberts- I did, he wasn't on the session. It must have been somebody else handling the session. Yeah that's possible. Because they know it was on Rip. Because I know Rip's very well and I know Webber, his right hand partner, because I used to play for all the big bands that came to their club which was low and low and low and low and low and low. And I know that's not a big band. I know that's not a big band. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I used to play for all the big bands that came to their club which was located on Dumain Street.
Yeah. Rip had a club. What was the name of it? San Jacinto was the name of the club. San Jacinto? Yeah.

Oh the San Jacinto club. Yeah. That's when he was booking, well he was booking big acts for Wake. Yeah I know Roberts used to book pretty big acts in town. Yeah. But I was going to do some session with Rip. I was going to work with Rip like I worked with Cosimo or Joe Asanto.

In the background which they always got greedy or something. I don't remember. Well all of them were like that. They were thick as thieves. Yeah well I think they'd be hurting more badly than I was. Well in the end they did.
